purpose: GliomaAI is a 3D Slicer scripted module that preprocesses brain MRI (RAS, SynthStrip, N4, z-score) and classifies glioma as LGG or HGG with bundled or downloaded 3D CNNs, optionally with Grad-CAM overlays. It targets researchers and runs locally on CPU.
summary: I read the CMake files, the module, and all PreProcessing code. I found no malicious behavior and no data exfiltration. Model downloads come from the author's GitHub release and are SHA-256 checked. The MIT license is present and the SynthStrip notice is included. The main problems are environment-related. Runtime `pip_install` of tensorflow==2.19.1 and nipreps-synthstrip has no user confirmation. nipreps-synthstrip very likely pulls torch from PyPI, which bypasses PyTorchUtils. TensorFlow also pins numpy and protobuf in Slicer's shared environment. There is also a real bug: `suffix` is undefined unless RAS is selected, so preprocessing crashes. The auto-generated test calls `process` with the wrong signature. I could not read the two large model files or the .ui file.
not_checked: Binary model files proposed_model_final.h5 and synthstrip.1.pt (content and provenance)
Release assets at v1.0.0 and their checksums
Actual dependency metadata of nipreps-synthstrip and tensorflow 2.19.1 on PyPI
Whether the SHA-256 listed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES matches the bundled file
Runtime behavior in Slicer; nothing was executed
